newsitem.title: USA: Barebright copper prices softer on weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Barebright copper prices softer on weak demand.

text.p: Barebright copper prices have eased in the last two weeks, as the scrap market begins to feel the pinch of the summer doldrums, scrap dealers and consumers said.

The softer prices came in conjuction with falling primary copper prices on COMEX, which usually coincides with a tightening of the scrap market. Scrap dealers often withdraw from the market when COMEX prices are weaker because their inventories become devalued.
But in this case, slack demand from the brass mills is putting pressure on prices.
Barebright prices were 1.50-3.00 cents under the COMEX spot price Thursday.
"Demand is usually weak this time of year," one brass mill executive said. "It's not anything structural within in the industry. It's just the summertime blues."
"There's plenty of scrap around," a scrap dealer said. "The COMEX price is simply not a factor right now."
The COMEX spot price has fallen 15 cents a pound since June 20.
In other copper scrap grades, #2 refinery differenials was steady at 22 cents under the COMEX December contract, Thursday

"The #2 market has been pretty weak lately, because there's been no appreciable export market," another scrap dealer said. "Hong Kong and China are the leading importers and neither has been very active lately."
The burnt market was unchanged at 5.00-6.00 cents under the COMEX December contract.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
